plan.geometry_notes: Flat 2D schematic, both panels side by side. LEFT PANEL centered at x=-3.5: apex carbon at (-3.5, 1.2, 0); two base carbons at bond length L=2.2 units placed symmetrically at ±(angle/2) below vertical, i.e. at (-3.5 ± L·sin(angle/2), 1.2 - L·cos(angle/2), 0). At 109° this gives base carbons at approximately (-5.4, -0.2) and (-1.6, -0.2). RIGHT PANEL centered at x=+3.5: equilateral triangle side 2.4 units, centered at (3.5, 0, 0), vertices at top (3.5, 1.39, 0), bottom-left (2.26, -0.69, 0), bottom-right (4.74, -0.69, 0). Dashed internuclear lines extend 1.0 units beyond each carbon atom on both ends. Orbital lobes: semi-transparent ellipsoids (opacity 0.55), semi-axes 0.65 along lobe axis × 0.32 × 0.32, pink #e88a9c. Overlap regions darken naturally where two semi-transparent lobes intersect — no separate overlap mesh needed. In the left panel at 109° the lobe axis coincides with the internuclear line; as angle decreases, rotate each lobe axis away from the internuclear line by misalignment = (109° - angle)/2, so lobes bend outward. In the right panel, lobes always point tangentially outward from the ring center, meeting outside each edge. Magenta arc radius 0.9 units at apex carbon, magenta #d6217a with arrowheads. Captions in bold black text below each panel. World extent: x from -6.5 to +6.5, y from -2.5 to +2.5. Colors: lobes #e88a9c at 0.55 opacity, dashed guides #111111, arc #d6217a, C labels black, captions black bold.
plan.notes: Both panels always visible — no show/hide toggle between them. Use THREE.Mesh with MeshPhongMaterial (transparent: true, opacity: 0.55, side: THREE.DoubleSide) for lobes so overlapping regions naturally appear darker. Model each lobe as SphereGeometry(1, 24, 16) scaled to (0.32, 0.65, 0.32) and oriented via quaternion. Dashed lines use LineDashedMaterial with dashSize 0.15, gapSize 0.1, call computeLineDistances(). The angle arc is a THREE.Line with ~40 segments plus two small cone arrowheads. On slider change, recompute left-panel carbon positions, lobe orientations, and arc span reactively. Misalignment guides (when toggled) draw thin orange lines from each carbon showing the angular offset between internuclear direction and lobe axis. Click raycasting on bond midpoint regions to highlight and display the misalignment angle as a floating label.

authoredPrompt: This figure places two orbital-overlap drawings side by side to contrast the bonding geometry of an open chain with that of a three-membered ring. On the left, three carbons lettered "C" sit at the ends and apex of a shallow V, with black dashed lines drawn through them marking the straight paths from nucleus to nucleus. Pink lobes of electron density project from each carbon along those dashed lines and meet head-on midway between neighboring atoms, the overlap regions shaded a deeper rose. A magenta double-headed arc spans the angle at the central carbon, labeled "109°". On the right, three carbons lettered "C" occupy the corners of a triangle. Dashed lines again mark the internuclear directions, but the pink lobes now emerge tilted away from them, so each pair meets outside the edge of the triangle rather than along the line joining the two carbons, leaving the interior open. Bold captions read "Typical alkane C−C bonds" and "Typical bent cyclopropane C−C bonds". Drawing the internuclear lines in both panels lets the reader compare where the lobes point against where the atoms actually lie, which accounts for why a ring squeezed to a 60 degree angle forms curved, poorly overlapped bonds that are weaker and more reactive than ordinary ones.
authoredInteractions:
- Slider for decreasing the C-C-C angle from a typical alkane value toward 60 degrees; the pink orbital lobes bend away from the dashed internuclear lines and the overlap patch shifts outward, showing why cyclopropane bonds are curved and strained.
- Toggle between Typical alkane C-C bonds and Typical bent cyclopropane C-C bonds; the same dashed nucleus-to-nucleus guides remain visible, making head-on overlap versus off-axis overlap the comparison to track.
authoredContext:
How can the hybrid-orbital model of bonding account for the large distortion of bond angles from the normal 109° tetrahedral value to 60° in cyclopropane? The answer is that cyclopropane has bent bonds. In an unstrained alkane, maximum bonding is achieved when two atoms have their overlapping orbitals pointing directly toward each other. In cyclopropane, though, the orbitals can’t point directly toward each other; instead, they overlap at a slight angle. The result is that cyclopropane bonds are weaker and more reactive than typical alkane bonds—255 kJ/mol (61 kcal/mol) for a C−C bond in cyclopropane versus 370 kJ/mol (88 kcal/mol) for a C−C bond in open-chain propane.

Orbital representations show typical alkane C-C bonds with 109 degrees angle and typical bent cyclopropane C-C bonds.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Flat 2D schematic (axis_screen_angles null). Open-chain view: apex carbon at origin (0,0,0); the two base carbons at bond length L=2.0 units placed symmetrically at ±(angle/2) below the horizontal, i.e. at (±L·sin(angle/2), -L·cos(angle/2), 0). Each C-C bond carries two teardrop lobes (ellipsoids, semi-axes ~0.62 along the lobe axis × 0.34 × 0.34) emanating from each carbon; at 109° the lobe axis coincides with the dashed internuclear line and the two lobes meet at the bond midpoint where a deeper-rose overlap ellipsoid (~0.30 radius) sits. As angle decreases, rotate each lobe axis away from the internuclear line by the misalignment (109°-angle)/2 so lobes bend and the overlap ellipsoid shifts outward off the dashed line. Ring view: equilateral triangle, side 2.6 units, centered at origin, carbons at the three corners; dashed lines join corners; lobes point tangentially (toward the circumcircle tangent / outward from ring center) so each pair overlaps OUTSIDE the corresponding edge, leaving the triangle interior empty. Magenta arc radius ~1.5 units centered at the apex carbon spanning the C-C-C angle, with arrowheads and a live degree label. Colors: lobes pink #e88a9c (semi-transparent ~0.85), overlap deeper rose #c0405e, dashed guides black #111111, angle arc + label magenta #d6217a, 'C' labels and captions black. World extent roughly ±3 X, ±2.5 Y.
interactionPlan.notes: Model each orbital lobe as a THREE.Mesh ellipsoid (SphereGeometry scaled) or a LatheGeometry teardrop, oriented via quaternion setFromUnitVectors from +Y to the lobe axis direction; recompute orientations and the overlap-ellipsoid position every time angleCC or bondType changes. Keep both panel geometries in the scene and show/hide on toggle rather than rebuilding. Draw dashed internuclear lines with LineDashedMaterial (computeLineDistances). Render the angle arc as a THREE.Line arc of ~40 segments plus two small cone arrowheads; update its span and the numeric label reactively. Use a flat front-on orthographic-like framing (no perspective depth) to match the source diagram.

Colors: lobes #e88a9c at 0.55 opacity, dashed guides #111111, arc #d6217a, C labels black, captions black bold.
plan.notes: Both panels always visible — no show/hide toggle between them. Use THREE.Mesh with MeshPhongMaterial (transparent: true, opacity: 0.55, side: THREE.DoubleSide) for lobes so overlapping regions naturally appear darker. Model each lobe as SphereGeometry(1, 24, 16) scaled to (0.32, 0.65, 0.32) and oriented via quaternion. Dashed lines use LineDashedMaterial with dashSize 0.15, gapSize 0.1, call computeLineDistances(). The angle arc is a THREE.Line with ~40 segments plus two small cone arrowheads. On slider change, recompute left-panel carbon positions, lobe orientations, and arc span reactively. Misalignment guides (when toggled) draw thin orange lines from each carbon showing the angular offset between internuclear direction and lobe axis. Click raycasting on bond midpoint regions to highlight and display the misalignment angle as a floating label.

evaluation.notes: A faithful, recognizable two-panel reproduction with correct primitives (C spheres, dashed internuclear lines, teardrop lobes, magenta arc), correct front-on orthographic projection, accurate labels/captions, and meaningful angle-squeeze slider plus step buttons and orbital tooltips; main weaknesses are lobe plumpness/shading and arc endpoint placement versus the source.
